newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-Taiwan July export orders seen up 7.41 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Taiwan July export orders seen up 7.41 pct.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists projected a year-on-year growth of 7.41 percent for Taiwan's export orders in July as electronics and information industries have entered their hot-sale season.
The figures are due to be released by the economics ministry at around 0230 GMT on August 21.
June's export orders rose 6.01 percent year-on-year.

Economists said they expected higher growth in July's export orders as Taiwan's information and electronics industries had gradually entered their hot-sale season.

"Taiwan's export orders should have higher growth starting from July especially after Intel cut microchip prices, a move that would trigger big increases in orders for Taiwan's electronics and information industries," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.

The Taiwan dollar's sharp depreciation against the U.S. dollar in late July should also boost Taiwan exporters' competitiveness worldwide, although the impact will be more significant in August, economists said.

HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang said orders for textile products should also rise as South Korean textiles makers, whose major plants entered maintenance period, transferred some orders to Taiwan.
